reference.notes:
I've filled in the four bodies in `packages/core/src/ticket.ts`, and every test passes: 52 in `ticket-content.test.ts`, 47 in `hidden-ticket-content/`, and 238 across the whole core suite. `npm test`, which also checks coverage, finishes cleanly, and `ticket.ts` is fully covered.

- **`normalizeSpecText`** splits lines on `\r\n`, `\r` or `\n`, trims the end of each line, joins them with `\n`, then trims both ends. This is the same as the private `normalize` in `packages/jira/src/spec.ts`.
- **`ticketSpecHash`** takes a SHA-256 hash, using `crypto.subtle`, of `JSON.stringify` applied to the three normalized strings, and returns it as lowercase hex. It's written the same way as Jira's `pricingSpecHash`, so it gives the same values, and it doesn't import `node:crypto`.
- **`clampTicketTitle`** trims the title and returns it unchanged if it fits in 255 characters. A longer title is cut to 254 characters, drops half an emoji if the cut splits one, trims trailing spaces and ends with `…`.
- **`ticketKey`** returns the trimmed `jiraKey` if it has any non-whitespace text. Otherwise it returns `#` plus the number, and throws the `RangeError` the spec gives if the number isn't a whole number from 1 up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.

**Not done:** the spec says `packages/core/src/index.ts` should gain `export * from "./ticket.js";`, but your instructions allow changes to `ticket.ts` only. I left `index.ts` alone, so the new functions can't yet be imported from the package's main entry point. The tests import `ticket.ts` directly, so they aren't affected. That one-line export is the remaining step.
